_readme: Combined Feats: pairs of feats that do something extra for anyone holding both.
The book's own term, from the Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide. A Combined Feat
is not a feat — nothing is chosen and no slot is spent. The benefit is simply on once both
halves are held, and off again the moment either is changed away.
Hand-maintained, like rules.json and skills.json — no importer writes this file.
The compendium already carries each one's wording, inside the description of the feats it
belongs to, under an 'Additional <Feat> Effects' heading that names the KotOR Campaign
Guide: 'Combined Feat (Running Attack): You can add your Dodge bonus to...'. That prose is
where `effect` below is copied from, so a card and the feat text above it agree word for
word. What the prose cannot say is whether you have the other half — that is what this
file is for, and why the six the summary spreadsheets listed arrived as twelve selectable
feats that each cost a slot and each demanded half of what they should. Those rows are
hidden in supplement.json; see the note there.
A half with no `spec` accepts any specialization — Weapon Focus completes its Combined
Feat whichever weapon group it was taken for. One that names a spec must match exactly.
To add one: give it an id, name both halves by feature id, and copy the effect from the
'Combined Feat (…)' line in the feats' own text. A test fails the build if a half names a
feature that does not exist, or if a feature carries such a line with no entry here.

combos.name: Cleave + Follow Through
effect: If you have the Follow Through Feat, you can move up to your speed before making the extra melee attack granted by the Cleave Feat.

combos.name: Combat Reflexes + Return Fire
effect: You may use the Return Fire Feat a number of times during an encounter equal to your Dexterity bonus, but no more than once during a given enemy's turn.

combos.name: Dodge + Charging Fire
effect: You reduce your penalty to your Reflex Defense against all opponents to -1 when making a ranged attack at the end of a Charge.

combos.name: Dodge + Running Attack
effect: You can add your Dodge bonus to your Reflex Defense against anyone who makes an Attack of Opportunity against you while using the Running Attack Feat.

combos.name: Force Training + Improved Disarm
effect: When you use the Force Disarm Force Power, you gain the +5 bonus from Improved Disarm on your Use the Force check as though you were making an attack roll.

combos.name: Quick Draw + Dual Weapon Mastery I
effect: You can draw or holster two weapons with a single Swift Action; you must have both hands free to draw both weapons, and each weapon must be able to be held in one hand.

combos.name: Quick Draw + Weapon Proficiency (lightsabers)
effect: You can draw and ignite your Lightsaber as a single Swift Action.

combos.name: Weapon Finesse + Weapon Focus
effect: When you are wielding a single one-handed weapon for which you have Weapon Focus, you can treat that weapon as a Light Weapon.
